Diplomierte Pflegefachpersonen HF/FH tragen die fachliche Verantwortung im gesamten Pflegeprozess. Sie erheben den Pflegebedarf, danach planen Sie die Massnahmen und werten die Ergebnisse aus. Job Summary The Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) provides operations support services and business solutions to the community of 10,000 House Members, Officers and staff.

The CAO organization comprises more than 650 technical and administrative staff working in a variety of areas, including information technology, finance, budget management, human resources, payroll, child care, food and vending, procurement, logistics and administrative counsel.

The Nurse position is located in the House of Representatives Child Care Center (HRCCC). The HRCCC has been providing full-day, year-round, quality childcare for children of the Members of Congress, staff, and House support personnel since 1987.

Accredited by the National Association for the Education of Young Children (NAEYC), the HRCCC is a developmentally based childcare program where staff work as partners with parents in the development of the whole child, including their physical, emotional, social, and cognitive development.

Our mission is to provide exceptional quality care and developmentally appropriate learning experiences in a safe, nurturing, and diverse environment to support the children and families of the House Community. This position serves as the Nurse and is considered a part of the Center Leadership Team and provides coaching services to staff.

The position does not have day-to-day supervisory/managerial responsibilities. Primary Duties and Responsibilities Provides onsite assessment of sick or injured children and staff. Provides care, first aid, and/or emergency care as needed. Identifies health problems and makes referrals for diagnosis and treatment.

Communicates information to families and other relevant parties, including primary care providers and emergency responders. Contacts families about symptoms requiring exclusion and provides guidelines for return. Tracks contagious illness occurrences throughout the House Child Care Center over time; sends notification of contagious illness.

Maintains and tracks children’s medical, dental, screening, and immunization records. Maintains accurate records and logs in a timely and organized fashion and meets all relevant deadlines; maintains data confidentiality. Maintains basic pharmacological knowledge and oversees the administration of medication.

Supervises special health care and food/nutrition plans and any accommodations necessary to serve children with special needs. Arranges care plan meetings with families and classroom teachers and supports classroom teachers with implementation of plans. Works with teachers to ensure all health needs are met within and away from the Center.

Develops familiarity and maintains compliance with all applicable legal requirements including House, Committee, CAO, and House Child Care Canter rules, practices, policies, and procedures. Develops, implements, and/or enforces laws, rules, regulations, procedures, and policies related to health and safety.

Provides feedback on policies and procedures as needed. Is an active leader in the House Child Care Center and the CAO; brings to Directors’ attention any relevant information or issues concerning or related to staff, children, and/or families.

Shows initiative towards the improvement of provided services by sharing ideas and participating in meetings. Assists in planning, developing, scheduling, and providing staff in-service training and evaluation of child care staff utilizing in-house and/or external resources.

Assesses knowledge of health, development, and safety in children and families; provides curriculum and training support as indicated. Performs other official duties and special projects as assigned.
Minimum Requirements Graduation from an accredited nursing program (Bachelor’s degree in Nursing and/or National Certified School Nurse credential preferred). Current registration as a registered nurse. Possession and maintenance of a BLS Certification for Healthcare Providers, including Infant/Child/Adult.

Minimum of 1 year relevant experience Experience working with sick or injured children; experience in pediatric nursing, community or school health, public health, emergency care, and triage preferred. Knowledge of basic infant and child health and development. Knowledge of health and safety standards for center-based child care settings.

Physical Requirements and Work Environment: This position is located in a school setting that is adequately heated, lighted, and ventilated. Normal safety precautions apply.

The work involves light physical activity and may include moderate physical activity, such as moving furniture and equipment, lifting and moving children, pushing cribs/carts/strollers, and participating in planned physical exercises with children (e.g., jumping, dancing, running).

The incumbent must be able to meet minimum physical requirements and work environment demands. Specifically, the incumbent must: Lift and/or move 50 pounds or more regularly. Stand, bend, stoop, squat, kneel, crouch, lift, twist, and grasp. Participate in moderate physical exercise for extended periods of time.

Be able to be outdoors for regular, prolonged activities in a variety of temperatures and weather conditions. Crouch or stand for extended periods of time. Possess hearing and visual capabilities necessary to monitor the environment and children’s wellbeing and promptly respond to emergency situations.

Participate in training to obtain/maintain awareness of and ensure adherence to all safety policies, procedures, and processes to include but not limited to allergies, other dietary restrictions, health conditions, and emergency response protocols.

Ability to successfully complete a physical exam and tuberculosis test (at the incumbent’s expense) prior to employment and annually thereafter (current documentation may not be older than 12 months). Security Requirements: Must successfully complete a criminal history records check.

Employee may be subject to drug testing in accordance with the CAO Drug Free Workplace Plan. Must successfully complete a Public Trust investigation with a Child Registry check.

Continued employment is contingent upon satisfactorily completing a criminal history records check (or other applicable security clearance) and a pre-employment drug-test (pre-identified position only).

Sie erheben den Pflegebedarf, danach planen Sie die Massnahmen und werten die Ergebnisse aus. Zudem steuern Sie die Abgabe der Medikamente, überwachen Vitalzeichen und erkennen Veränderungen früh. Damit sichern Sie Tag für Tag die Qualität der Pflege.

Ausländische Diplome brauchen dafür eine [Anerkennung durch das Schweizerische Rote Kreuz (SRK)](https://www.redcross.ch/de/srk-anerkennung). To provide safe, high-quality, evidence-based nursing care to students and emergency response to staff, and visitors within an international and boarding school environment during the main school and also the Summer Camp.
The School Nurse is responsible for assessing and managing illness and injury, providing emergency and first-aid care, administering medications and treatments, coordinating with families and external healthcare professionals, and supporting the physical, emotional, and mental wellbeing of students.
The role also carries significant responsibility for safeguarding and child protection, ensuring that student welfare and safety remain central to all aspects of nursing practice.

Professional Nursing Practice
Practise in accordance with Swiss nursing regulations, applicable professional standards, Croix-Rouge requirements, and NMC guidance (if applicable).
Provide evidence-based, patient-centred nursing care.
Maintain confidentiality and comply with applicable Swiss data protection requirements.
Maintain professional boundaries and uphold high standards of professional conduct.
Participate in continuing professional development, mandatory training, and safeguarding education.
Maintain competence in emergency response, first aid, medication administration, and relevant clinical procedures.
Clinical Nursing Care
Provide nursing care to students, staff, and visitors during scheduled shifts.
Assess and manage acute and chronic illnesses, injuries, and health conditions.
Conduct nursing assessments and develop appropriate care plans.
Monitor students' health and recognise signs of deterioration requiring escalation or referral.
Provide first aid and emergency care in accordance with relevant Swiss and Croix-Rouge standards.
Refer students to doctors, hospitals, emergency services, or other healthcare professionals when clinically appropriate.
Administer prescribed medications and treatments safely and maintain accurate medication records.
Support vaccination programmes and infection prevention and control procedures in accordance with applicable Swiss guidance.
Provide health advice and appropriate emotional support to students.
Maintain accurate and contemporaneous electronic medical records.
On Call and Overnight Nursing
Remain on call and available throughout the scheduled shift to respond to student health needs.
Respond promptly to urgent and unexpected illnesses, injuries, and medical concerns.
Provide overnight nursing care and observation to unwell students.
Monitor students in the Health Centre and, when required, coordinate care with boarding/house staff.
Escalate concerns appropriately to senior clinical staff, parents, doctors, emergency services, or other healthcare professionals.
Provide clear and accurate clinical handovers to ensure continuity of care.
Maintain calm, professional decision-making during urgent and potentially stressful situations.
Individual Student Care
Develop and maintain individual health and care plans in collaboration with students, parents, house staff, wellbeing teams, and external healthcare professionals.
Consider students' capacity to consent to treatment in accordance with applicable professional and legal requirements.
Communicate with parents/guardians regarding significant illness, injury, treatment, and follow-up while respecting confidentiality.
Support students with ongoing medical, physical, emotional, and wellbeing needs.
Promote student independence and encourage appropriate self-management of health conditions.
Safeguarding and Child Protection
Actively promote and follow the school's Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy.
Maintain awareness of indicators of abuse, neglect, exploitation, and other safeguarding concerns.
Record safeguarding concerns accurately, objectively, and promptly.
Report concerns immediately through the school's established safeguarding procedures and to the Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL).
Maintain appropriate professional boundaries with students at all times.
Participate in regular safeguarding and child-protection training.
Contribute to a culture of vigilance, safety, and student welfare across the school community.
Promote healthy lifestyles and positive health behaviours among students.

s.h: Provide age-appropriate health advice and education.
s.t:
Support school-wide wellbeing and pastoral initiatives.
Contribute to health and wellbeing discussions, workshops, clinics, and educational activities.
Keep up to date with relevant health promotion, adolescent health, and safeguarding guidance.
Medication and Clinical Resources
Safely administer, store, monitor, and document medications in accordance with prescriptions, care plans, and applicable regulations.
Maintain appropriate medication records and stock control.
Monitor expiry dates and ensure medications are stored securely.
Maintain and restock first-aid kits and emergency medical supplies.
Ensure appropriate storage and disposal of clinical waste and medical materials.
Assist with ordering and distribution of medical supplies and equipment.
Administration and Documentation
Maintain accurate, confidential, and up-to-date medical records.
Record all clinical consultations, assessments, treatments, medications, and interventions in the school's health database.
Complete accident, incident, and medico-legal documentation when required.
Support insurance-related documentation and reporting.
Assist with Health Centre administration and daily operational requirements.
Maintain appropriate records relating to medical supplies, expenditure, and resources.
Health, Safety and Risk Management
Promote health and safety within the Health Centre and wider school environment.
Contribute to health-related risk assessments for school trips, residential activities, sports, events, and other activities.
Provide advice regarding medical considerations and appropriate health precautions for school activities.
Ensure Health Centre procedures comply with relevant health and safety requirements.
Support infection prevention and control measures throughout the school.
Communication and Multidisciplinary Collaboration
Work collaboratively with nurses, doctors, boarding/house staff, teachers, pastoral teams, wellbeing staff, safeguarding staff, and school leadership.
Liaise with parents and guardians regarding student healthcare needs.
Coordinate care with external doctors, hospitals, therapists, specialists, and other healthcare professionals.
Participate in multidisciplinary meetings relating to student health, welfare, and safeguarding.
Provide effective clinical handovers to ensure continuity and safety of care.
Maintain confidentiality and professionalism in all verbal and written communication.
Working Hours
Position with scheduled shifts that may include day, evening, night, weekend, and other unsocial hours.
On call responsibilities are incorporated within the scheduled shift, requiring the nurse to remain available and responsive to student health needs throughout the assigned duty period.
